change_and_selector_rules: Inventory digest is a byte/source-context binding, not the formal-impact predicate. Snapshot commit IDs alone are outside SourceContent only under the declared snapshot role; immutable origin commits and dependency revisions remain in content. Keep full refs/membership separately and retain current adapter paired-snapshot normalization exactly, not for origins.

Comparable changed type-record bytes classify formal_statement_changed. Actual compiler/options/print/dependency/runtime context change classifies comparison_unknown plus revalidation even with equal type bytes. Scope/import or raw manifest contract change also seeds revalidation. Source/selector content changes alter inventory digest; no semantic equivalence is inferred.

A module edit can be proof_body_changed only with actual accepted declaration AND proof selectors on both sides, equal declaration-slice bytes and target-type bytes/context, and equality of the two whole module byte strings after removing the complete accepted proof intervals (sort intervals by start; nonoverlap required). This is a conservative source classification, not proof validity or alignment acceptance. All other target declarations/uses and imported context must remain accounted for.

The exact changed proof bytes/module/slice identities still change this inventory digest. A required manifest refresh or scope/dependency delta adds its independent revalidation reason and is never suppressed by proof_body_changed. The current raw-manifest binding is deliberately conservative.

Selector-only change (including offset change, addition or known absence/loss) changes selector content/digest and classifies formal_selector_changed; it never alone asserts changed printed type or failed/stale kernel. An actual module edit with either accepted declaration/proof selector absent or unqualified remains formal_source_changed_unscoped, never guessed proof-only. Unknown acceptance/source join also preserves unresolved coverage.

Execution-only failure/loss is evidence_loss_impact, not a semantic type delta. A missing newly collected type yields an unresolved diagnostic inventory, not formal_statement_changed by null comparison. Source/type/scope join loss can separately require semantic revalidation under the existing conservative policy. Preserve all original groups and separate union impact rules.

formal_inventory_hash_contract.one_formula: formal_inventory_sha256 = lowercase_hex(SHA256(CanonicalASCII(InventoryCore))). CanonicalASCII is precisely lexical_rules.json: sorted object keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=true, no nonfinite values, ASCII bytes and NO trailing newline. No prefix/suffix, extra digest wrapper or raw TargetStatement is hashed.
projection_and_qualification: Resolve candidate inventory only at S from complete authenticated native manifest/target/module/scope/source membership and actual qualified original target-type records. Base uses identical rules at B for comparison. No raw TargetStatement, native_context, type_record.log_ref, capture/run/artifact/member IDs, attempt, event, acquisition, timestamp, evidence_revision or terminal message is copied into InventoryCore.

Project each actual target once. Read exact native format/repository/manifest/package/name, not graph labels. Derive SourceContent, type slice content, compiler/build/dependency/runtime content, accepted selectors and scope inputs by the closed forms above. Preserve source/control/compiler/runtime provenance plus ALL complete raw records in separate custody fields.

A required content field that is unavailable/unauthenticated/unsupported is null and its exact field name appears in unresolved_fields; a paired type hash/byte size is both null and lists both field names. Identity enumeration failure means core absent. Explicit known-absent accepted formal selectors use selector:null, not fabricated offsets. Unknown mapping/acceptance remains a separate coverage failure even if a diagnostic content core can be serialized.

Diagnostic partial cores may be byte-hashed as diagnostic_inventory_sha256 only. formal_inventory_sha256 is null unless enumeration is complete, every required content field has its closed qualified value and all unresolved_fields arrays are empty. A content digest alone never satisfies mapping, native positive execution, request freshness, attempt/custody, alignment authority or preservation. Known null selectors are not proof-only evidence.

No custody acquisition detail participates in this hash; recollection with new run/attempt/log offsets but exactly the same source and target-record bytes produces identical InventoryCore. A later acquisition never rebinds old K to S. Existing independently qualified same-S records may remain preserved; a failed new attempt does not erase them or create a new positive execution claim.

Collector emits the core and digest; detached Revalidation.formal_inventory_sha256 is EXACTLY this candidate digest; offline verifier independently projects the core from authenticated raw records, compares canonical core bytes and recomputes the same one formula. Null/diagnostic digests cannot be accepted in Revalidation. Reject a supplied inconsistent core/hash rather than selecting one interpretation.

lexical_rules.identities: Git SHA40 lowercase hex; SHA256 lowercase64hex; native IDs positive ASCII decimal strings. Paths normalized safe repository/bundle-relative, never supplied URLs. Exact nullable values preserved.
lexical_rules.json: Closed fields, duplicate/nonfinite/trailing/deep/oversized/type-coerced input refuses. Exact integer excludes Boolean. Canonical JSON is sort_keys=True,separators=(comma,colon),ensure_ascii=True,allow_nan=False, ASCII, no newline.
lexical_rules.unknown: Absent authoritative source/capability is explicit UNRESOLVED/null with reason, never inferred mapping, attempt, acceptance or PASS.

read_extent_notice: All new product interfaces/types are proposed, not historical accepted ABI. Existing adapter v1 and native formats stay unchanged. Source/runtime/collector/review custody remain separate predicates.
regression_rules: Historical-original adapter projection retains old formal records, exact old review refs and original bytes. Candidate projection retains candidate records. Single expected native context is explicitly labeled; old/cross-repository kernel states are not globally refreshed.

For multiple native contexts, any extra candidate projections retain all whole-group uses; never partition one immutable original alignment group to hide a held use. Native local kernel proof and graph-source join remain separate, including unknown Math bridge.

Semantic fingerprints cover exactly every graph node and include authoritative mapping, formal statement/type/options/dependency content, scope/manifest contract and appropriate source selectors. Unknown nodes have explicit unknown rows and coverage cannot PASS.

Invoke independently pinned reverse_impact_between on actual old/new graphs and semantic snapshots; union all old/new edges. Keep returned hold clone derived. Union its semantic impacts with existing adapter regression.

Comparable type-byte changes are formal_statement_changed, not semantic-equivalence judgement. Changed compiler/dependency/print context is comparison_unknown plus revalidation. Missing accepted formal selectors means module change is unscoped, never guessed proof-only.

Execution-only failed/skipped/missing/stale/negative/attempt-unknown native evidence lowers native axis and fails required positive predicate. Separate evidence-loss impact cannot alone fabricate changed statement, stale semantic alignment or affected original review refs.

Select original review refs from authenticated old explicit node-target links, union downstream all-edge impact, group by all six GitRef fields, retain deleted records and surviving whole-group uses. Missing mapping/ref remains unresolved; no fabricated ID.

Qualified detached successor review covers every affected original group in exact candidate context; retain original stale inventory and link replacements. Fresh kernel/source is not semantic revalidation.
